papers.title: Unsupervised functional stage detection from EEG using topological data analysis.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a topological data analysis (TDA)-based feature engineering approach for unsupervised EEG functional stage detection, combined with a quick state-detecting algorithm (QSDA). Applied to meditation and sleep EEG recordings, the method produced well-separated stage boundaries and remained robust on noisy data, suggesting TDA can complement or outperform spectral features in some settings.

papers.title: BMAL1 Overexpression in the SCN Confers Protection Against Anxiety-Like Behaviors of Chronic Sleep Restricted-Mice.
papers.summary: In 5-week-old male mice, chronic sleep restriction induced anxiety-like behaviors and impaired mPFC synaptic plasticity, with BMAL1 overexpression in the SCN further reducing open-arm/social-chamber exploration while restoring BDNF signaling via MAPK-linked inflammatory, SOD, and MDA changes.

papers.title: Comparable memory retention following brief periods of wakeful rest and napping: A pilot study.
papers.summary: In a pilot study with 90 participants, 20-min wakeful rest and napping produced comparable general item memory retention, both better than gameplay, with similar FN400/LPC ERP patterns and partially generalizable old/new neural decoding across rest and nap states.

papers.title: Spontaneous slow waves index multiple dimensions of recovery in Disorders of Consciousness
papers.summary: In 236 DoC patients, higher-amplitude and steeper spontaneous slow waves indexed greater consciousness and better one-year recovery, with slow-wave features above-chance classification of MCS- and MCS+ versus UWS and structural associations to subcortico-cortical projection integrity.

papers.title: Subthalamic nucleus beta oscillations and sleep disorders in Parkinson's disease: A new perspective on deep brain stimulation regulation mechanisms and circuits.
papers.summary: This review proposes that aberrant subthalamic nucleus beta oscillations disrupt sleep microarchitecture in Parkinson's disease, and that STN-DBS improves sleep by suppressing pathological beta synchronization, restoring network dynamics, and modulating arousal circuits.

papers.title: Multimodal LLMs Can Learn to Read Brain Signals: A Vision--Language Model for Unified Multi-Task EEG Decoding
papers.summary: BraVista, a vision-language framework encoding multichannel EEG as structured images and instruction-conditioned tuning of a general-domain VLM, achieved strong multi-task performance across sleep staging, emotion recognition, cognitive workload, and abnormal EEG detection, with EEG-to-image representation critical and gradual degradation under noise.

papers.title: High arousal threshold is associated with impaired sustained attention in patients with obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
papers.summary: In 97 OSA patients, high arousal threshold (ArTH) was associated with impaired sustained attention on the Psychomotor Vigilance Task, including higher lapse probability and slower mean 1/reaction time. Linear trends linked lower ArTH scores to worse sustained attention after adjusting for confounders.

papers.title: Circadian misalignment and low-grade inflammation: Failure of temporal gating by the molecular clock.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes molecular, animal, and human evidence to propose that circadian misalignment impairs temporal gating of innate immunity by the molecular clock, particularly via REV-ERBα and BMAL1 regulation of NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasome. It highlights that controlled human protocols show modest increases in 24-hour high-sensitivity C-reactive protein even when sleep loss is controlled, but causal inference remains incomplete.

papers.title: An Intensified Training Period Reduces REM Sleep but this Decline Can Be Mitigated by Ketone Ester Supplementation.
papers.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
papers.summary: In a double-blind study of 24 trained male athletes undergoing 7 weeks of intensified training, ketone ester supplementation prevented the decline in REM sleep seen in controls from pre- to post-training. Both groups showed improved sleep efficiency and reduced wakefulness after sleep onset from pre to mid-training, but only controls showed a subsequent decrease in total REM sleep.

papers.title: Considerations and guidelines for photic measurement in field studies of the physiological effects of light.
papers.summary: This review outlines pre-ocular, ocular, and post-ocular factors and provides practical guidelines and a standard operating procedure for measuring light exposure in field studies of non-visual physiological effects. It discusses trade-offs of different measurement approaches and identifies future directions and remaining challenges.

papers.title: Multisensory perceptual decision-making persists as alertness fades, even in the absence of an overt response
papers.summary: Participants performed an audio-tactile spatial localisation task during EEG across the wake-sleep transition to examine multisensory perceptual decision-making. Drowsiness slowed responses and increased omissions but accuracy remained largely intact, tactile congruency and conflict effects persisted, behavioural modelling showed slower evidence accumulation and increased decision boundaries, and multisensory congruency decoding was no longer reliable during drowsiness despite robust stimulus- and response-related neural decodability.

papers.title: The Case for Kinases: a Phosphorylation Driven Model for Circadian Temperature Compensation in Neurospora crassa.
papers.summary: Using novel alleles and quantitative proteomics, this study investigated the genetic relationship between Casein Kinase I (CK-1a) and Casein Kinase II (CKA) in regulating temperature compensation of the Neurospora circadian clock. The results support a phosphorylation-driven model in which decreasing CK1 activity on FRQ with increasing temperature is countered by increasing CK2 activity, shaping the FRQ phosphorylation landscape to maintain period length.

papers.title: Effects of environmental enrichment on outcomes of in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer in ICR mice.
papers.journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science
papers.summary: This study evaluated the effects of environmental enrichment (EE) on mother mice and pups after in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer (IVF-ET). EE did not significantly affect litter sizes but tended to increase weaning rate, increased body weight gain in male and female pups by 11% and 6%, respectively, and tended to decrease fecal cortisol during lactation.

papers.title: Development of Rest-Activity Rhythms in Infancy and Their Disruption in Infantile Epileptic Spasms Syndrome.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The study characterized rest-activity rhythm (RAR) maturation in healthy infants and compared RARs in infants with infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (IESS) to age-matched controls. In 891 actigraphy recordings from 333 healthy infants, RAR height, interdaily stability, entropy, and fractal complexity increased with age while fragmentation decreased; infants with IESS (n=11) showed marked reductions in RAR height, interdaily stability, entropy, and fractal complexity compared to controls.

papers.title: Spectrally-resolved transfer entropy in resting-state SEEG reveals epileptogenic and non-epileptogenic communication in adults and children with refractory epilepsy.
papers.summary: The study characterized spectrally-resolved directed communication between seizure onset zones (SOZ) and non-involved zones (NIZ) using resting-state SEEG transfer entropy in 21 adults and 18 children with refractory epilepsy. It found longer NIZ-to-SOZ median delays in adults than children (87.9 ms vs 68.0 ms) and distinct frequency profiles for intra-SOZ links, while inter-regional NIZ-to-SOZ interactions lacked a distinct spectral profile.

papers.title: Neurophysiological signatures of latent brain vulnerability in perioperative neurocognitive disorders: integrating EEG, cerebral oximetry, and processed EEG.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on EEG, NIRS/cerebral oximetry, and processed EEG/BIS as candidate objective markers of perioperative brain vulnerability, describing patterns such as reduced alpha activity, burst suppression, cerebral oxygen desaturation, and impaired autoregulation. It concludes that these signals may aid risk stratification and phenotyping but are not yet a validated early-warning system, pending prospective monitor-guided trials.

papers.title: Exploring the Reconfiguration Effects of Physical Fatigue on the Gradient Space of Brain Function Based on EEG.
papers.summary: The study examined how physical fatigue reorganizes the low-dimensional structure of EEG functional connectivity using PCA, Laplacian eigenmaps, and diffusion maps in 30 male participants who completed a treadmill test to exhaustion. Fatigue induced frequency-, region-, component-, and method-specific changes, with PCA showing increased beta-band G1 over central scalp and decreased over occipital, and the central beta-band ΔG1 positively correlated with exercise duration (r=0.50, p=0.004).

papers.title: High-frequency oscillations arise through distinct mechanisms in models of α- synucleinopathy and channelopathy-induced epilepsy.
papers.summary: The study quantified cortical high-frequency oscillations (HFOs, 250-500 Hz) and interictal spikes in a transgenic α-synucleinopathy model (A53T mice, a model of dementia with Lewy bodies) and a channelopathy-induced epilepsy model (Kcna1-/- mice). Both models showed elevated HFOs across vigilance states, but A53T mice had more HFOs and interictal spikes, with higher frequency and longer duration HFOs, and HFOs were most prevalent during non-REM sleep in A53T mice, suggesting distinct mechanisms.

papers.title: Effects of acute sleep deprivation on individuals across different APOE genotypes: a randomized controlled trial protocol.
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial protocol describes a study to assess the effects of 24-hour acute sleep deprivation on plasma Alzheimer's disease biomarkers (Aβ42, Aβ40, t-tau, p-tau181, p-tau217, NfL, GFAP) in 60 healthy young adults stratified by APOE genotype (ε3/ε3, ε4 carriers, ε2 carriers). It aims to test APOE genotype-dependent biomarker responses and includes exploratory proteomics, metabolomics, and PET/MRI outcomes.

papers.title: Circadian and Sex-Specific Responses to Alternaria alternata in Allergic Airway Inflammation
papers.summary: In a preclinical mouse model, Alternaria alternata-induced allergic airway inflammation, airway hyperresponsiveness, and epithelial barrier disruption were found to depend on circadian time and sex, with female mice showing greater inflammation at ZT0 and males at ZT12. The study links these responses to IL-33, ILC2/Th2 accumulation, STAT activation, and altered clock protein expression, suggesting chronotherapeutic approaches for asthma.

papers.title: Vitamin B6 augments antidepressant activity of venlafaxine by restoring cortical EEG oscillations, behavior and oxidative biomarkers in chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced model of depression-like behavior.
papers.summary: The study investigated whether vitamin B6 (Vit B6) enhances the antidepressant efficacy of venlafaxine (VEN) in a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) model of depression-like behavior in C57BL/6 mice. Combined treatment restored behavioral performance, reduced oxidative stress markers (decreased MDA, increased catalase), and restored cortical EEG oscillations (attenuated theta hyperactivity, increased alpha and gamma power), suggesting a promising combination strategy.

papers.title: Developmental variation in resting-state EEG spectral correlates of response inhibition in children and adolescents.
papers.summary: The study examined associations between resting-state EEG spectral indices and response inhibition in 1654 children and adolescents aged 6-18, and tested whether these associations varied with age. Higher delta power, theta power, and theta/beta ratio (TBR) were associated with poorer response inhibition, whereas higher alpha power, beta power, alpha/theta ratio (ATR), and beta/theta ratio (BTR) were associated with better response inhibition; age moderated the associations for delta power, beta power, ATR, and BTR.

papers.title: Tri-Stream Disentangled Network with Adaptive Dual-Space Fusion for Electroencephalography-Based Image Reconstruction on THINGS-EEG2.
papers.summary: The paper presents a protocol for the Tri-Stream Disentangled Network (TDE-Net), a computational framework for EEG-based image reconstruction that organizes EEG into raw anchor, functional graph, and temporal semantic streams. Evaluated on THINGS-EEG2, TDE-Net achieved a mean CLIP pairwise identification accuracy of 0.8135 across 10 participants.

papers.title: Olfactory impairment and probable REM sleep behavior disorder in Parkinson's disease: clinical relevance to the single- and dual-hit hypotheses.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 201 Parkinson's disease patients, probable RBD (pRBD) and anosmia co-occurrence was examined relative to single- and dual-hit hypotheses. Anosmia was associated with cognitive impairment in pRBD-negative but not pRBD-positive participants, and significant anosmia-by-pRBD interactions were found for motor severity and cognition, suggesting that combined olfactory and pRBD assessment may refine clinical phenotyping.

papers.title: Music-evoked EEG signals for mental health assessment using two- and three-class classification.
papers.summary: This preliminary study used EEG recordings from 48 participants during music and no-music sessions with mental health questionnaires to classify mental fatigue and multi-output anxiety, depression, and stress using a deep residual MLP. Binary classification achieved 72.92% accuracy in the music condition vs 58.33% without music, with 96.67% recall in music; multi-output classification showed 93.75% accuracy for stress but low AUC (35.56%), and anxiety and depression were harder to classify.

papers.title: Feature-Engineering Strategies for EEG-Based ADHD Classification in Children: A Controlled Benchmark of Expert, LLM-Guided and Full-Space Comparators
papers.summary: This benchmark compared expert-reconstructed, LLM-guided, and full-space feature strategies for EEG-based ADHD classification in 77 children under leakage-controlled subject-level validation. Expert-reconstructed features with random forest achieved 71.4% accuracy in LOOCV, while no consistent advantage was found for LLM-guided features, and strict artifact gating reduced accuracy below the no-information rate.

papers.title: Associations of Sleep Duration and Adherence to Age-Specific Sleep Recommendations with Body Fat and Related Anthropometric Characteristics in Children and Adolescents.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 1402 children and adolescents aged 3-16 years in Kraków examined associations between parent-reported sleep duration, adherence to age-specific sleep recommendations, and detailed anthropometric adiposity measures. Longer sleep duration was consistently but modestly associated with lower body mass, BMI, adiposity, circumferences, and waist-to-height ratio; adherence to sleep recommendations was not independently associated with adiposity after adjustment for age.

papers.title: Sleep restriction induces histoarchitectural and cellular remodeling in the rat distal colon: a peripheral consequence of circadian disruption.
authors: Gláucia Eloisa Munhoz de Lion Siervo
papers.summary: Rats exposed to 21 days of sleep restriction showed increased mucosal thickness, crypt depth, goblet cell depletion, mast cell hyperplasia, and enteric neuro-glial remodeling in the distal colon, without macroscopic lesions. These findings suggest that intestinal remodeling is a peripheral consequence of circadian disruption.

papers.title: Rethinking the lexicon of REM sleep behavior disorder: a two-axis proposal.
papers.summary: This review proposes a new two-axis lexicon for REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) that integrates a pathophysiological axis and a clinical axis to classify polysomnography-confirmed RBD, arguing that current terms such as 'clinically isolated RBD' and 'secondary RBD' are misleading especially for biomarker-based definitions. The framework aims to improve patient characterization in clinical and research settings.

papers.title: Impact of obstructive sleep apnea on outcomes of acute respiratory distress syndrome: propensity matched analysis of a national cohort.
papers.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
papers.summary: This retrospective propensity-matched analysis of a national inpatient cohort compared outcomes of ARDS patients with and without preexisting obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Among 9405 OSA patients matched to 9206 controls, OSA was independently associated with 34% lower odds of in-hospital mortality, shorter length of stay by 2.0 days, lower total hospitalization charges by $74,601, and lower rates of invasive mechanical ventilation and tracheostomy.

papers.title: Circadian dysregulation of leptin and its role in skin inflammation and obesity: an integrative perspective.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on circadian leptin dysregulation linking meal timing and sleep disruption to obesity-associated skin inflammation, with a focus on psoriasis. It concludes that circadian leptin misalignment may represent a plausible upstream pathway, but direct causal evidence remains limited.

papers.title: The role of sleep and circadian rhythms in intervertebral disc degeneration.
papers.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
papers.summary: This narrative review examines bidirectional associations between sleep/circadian disturbances and intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD), proposing five interconnected pathways including peripheral clock disruption and inflammation. It identifies CBT-I, exogenous melatonin, and morning bright light therapy as interventions with dual benefits for sleep and IDD.

papers.title: Determination of central pain modulation biomarkers to characterise patients with cancer and refractory pain: protocol for a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: This paper presents a protocol for a multicenter, cross-sectional, case-control study aiming to identify and validate central pain modulation biomarkers using quantitative sensory testing (QST) and EEG in patients with cancer pain. The study will include at least 470 ambulatory patients (313 with oncological pain, 157 without) and will use statistical modeling and machine learning to characterize pain modulation and its moderators.

papers.title: Effect of Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation on Postoperative Delirium in Older Patients Undergoing Carotid Endarterectomy: A Randomized Controlled Study.
papers.journal: Neuromodulation : journal of the International Neuromodulation Society
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 65 older patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy, transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) significantly reduced the incidence and severity of postoperative delirium (POD) compared to control. TEAS also lowered optic nerve sheath diameter, Athens Insomnia Scale scores, and TNF-α levels, while increasing BDNF levels, suggesting links to reduced intracranial hypertension, improved sleep, and suppressed inflammation.

papers.title: Pulmonary Function, Functional Capacity, Voice, and Sleep in Post-COVID-19 Individuals With and Without Inspiratory Muscle Weakness.
papers.journal: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 28 post-COVID-19 adults, those with inspiratory muscle weakness (MIP <70% predicted) had higher fatigue prevalence, worse vocal handicap (VHI) and vocal fatigue (VFI) scores, and lower maximum phonation times for /s/ and /z/ compared to those without weakness. Lower inspiratory muscle strength correlated with greater vocal fatigue, highlighting an association between respiratory muscle function and voice outcomes.

papers.title: Patient and caregiver burden after hospitalization with severe viral lower respiratory tract disease: results from a real-world survey in Europe, the US and Japan.
papers.summary: A real-world cross-sectional survey of 1071 patients hospitalized with severe viral lower respiratory tract disease 6-24 months prior and 104 caregivers across Europe, the US, and Japan found persistent physical and mental health burdens, with 66% of patients reporting mental health impact and 50% of caregivers reporting moderate-to-extreme sleep impact. Mean EQ-5D-5L was 0.72 and caregiver Zarit Burden Interview score was 15.0, indicating notable post-discharge quality-of-life and productivity impairments.

papers.title: Melatonin protects keratinocytes from diesel-derived PM2.5-induced damage by suppressing JNK/p38 MAPK signaling and caspase activation.
papers.summary: In HaCaT keratinocytes and hairless mice, melatonin attenuated diesel-derived PM2.5-induced oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis by scavenging ROS and inhibiting JNK/p38 MAPK phosphorylation and caspase-9/3 activation. Co-treatment with pan-caspase, JNK, or p38 MAPK inhibitors did not further enhance melatonin's anti-apoptotic effect, suggesting melatonin acts through these pathways.

papers.title: Appropriateness/inappropriateness of access to an in-hospital rehabilitation program for patients with respiratory disease.
papers.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
papers.summary: Analysis of 10 years of hospitalization records from seven Italian rehabilitation centers found high overall appropriateness (73-87% across items) for in-hospital respiratory rehabilitation admissions, with only 2.8% deemed inappropriate. Chronic respiratory failure patients had the highest appropriateness (>78% across items) and the lowest inappropriateness (0.7%), while dyspnea and OSAS subgroups had lower appropriateness.

papers.title: Loneliness, problematic digital media use, and nutritional-metabolic vulnerability in adolescents from single-parent households: an integrative review of eating- and sleep-related pathways.
papers.summary: This integrative review synthesized evidence on loneliness and problematic digital media use as they relate to eating- and sleep-related behaviors in adolescents from single-parent households, proposing a contextual-behavioral vulnerability model. Direct evidence on single-parent adolescents was limited and mainly focused on family meals and weight outcomes, while broader evidence linked loneliness and digital media use to emotional eating, sleep disruption, and poor diet quality, with links to metabolic outcomes remaining largely indirect.

papers.title: Factors Associated with the Health Status of Caregivers of Community-dwelling Older Adults with Dementia in Japan: The Toyama Dementia Survey.
keywords: behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia
papers.summary: This cross-sectional survey of 75 caregiver-care recipient pairs in Toyama, Japan, found that 40% of family caregivers of older adults with dementia experienced physical health problems and 37.3% experienced mental health problems. Caregiver age 80 years or older was significantly associated with physical health problems (adjusted OR 13.46), and male caregivers reported more sleep deprivation than female caregivers.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
